chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abd al-A'la, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ask God for sufficiency in the world and well-being, and in the Hereafter, for forgiveness and Paradise.

key_terms.الجنة: Paradise, the Garden of eternal bliss promised to the believers
key_terms.العافية: Well-being, health, safety, and protection from affliction in all its forms
key_terms.الغنى: Sufficiency, freedom from want; not excess wealth but adequate provision and contentment
key_terms.المغفرة: Divine forgiveness; the effacement of sins by God's mercy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say to ask from God for this world and the next?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs believers to supplicate to God for two essential gifts: ease and well-being in worldly life, and forgiveness with entry into Paradise in the afterlife. This teaching reflects the Quranic supplication 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter' (2:201), contextualizing it as a practical directive for daily supplication. The pairing of 'sufficiency' (al-ghina) with 'well-being' (al-'afiya) emphasizes that worldly good encompasses both material adequacy and bodily health, while the ultimate aspiration in the Hereafter is divine pardon and eternal reward.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Abdul Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the ease in the world and the health, and regarding the Hereafter, the Forgiveness and the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Ask Allah to grant you (financial) self-sufficiency and good health in this world, forgiveness and paradise in the hereafter.’”
